extracted.intended_audience: researchers, policymakers, program officers, and practitioners interested in grant peer review processes (e.g., NIH study section chairs, review officers, and grant reviewers)
extracted.subtask_description: Empirical mixed-methods analysis of how discussion and 'Score Calibration Talk' (SCT) in grant peer review meetings relate to score changes, within-panel convergence, and between-panel variability. Includes operational definitions, coding rules, quantitative reliability/variability metrics, and suggested interventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Krippendorff's α reliability thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: A value of α ≥ 0.8 is considered ‘reliable’, and values between 0.67 and 0.8 are considered suitable for drawing ‘tentative conclusions’ (Krippendorff 2004).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Krippendorff's α to assess interrater reliability for coded measures and for assessing agreement on scores (intra-panel and inter-panel). Interpret negative α as slight disagreement. Report α for different score aggregations (preliminary reviewer, final reviewer, final panel).

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary Reviewer Scores / Final Reviewer Scores / Final Panel Scores (operational outcome metrics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Preliminary Reviewer Scores: independent scores assigned by individual reviewers before the meeting; Final Reviewer Scores: scores assigned by reviewers after discussion; Final Panel Scores: aggregate (average) panel-level score for an application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat these as primary dependent variables for analyses of discussion effects. Compute averages per panel, and use these in range and agreement comparisons. Note: only 'discussed' applications (top ~50%) receive final scores and are included in final-score analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Range as a measure of score variability
rubrics_metrics.description: The range (max - min) of reviewer or panel average scores is used to quantify variability within panels (range_prelim, range_final) and between panels (range PanelPrelim, range PanelFinal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare ranges before and after discussion to assess convergence/divergence. Paired comparisons of ranges (within applications across conditions) illuminate shifts in spread. Report mean and SD of ranges when summarizing results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paired-samples t-test for pre/post range comparisons
rubrics_metrics.description: Use paired-samples t-tests to compare the range of panels' Preliminary Reviewer Scores with the range of panels' Final Reviewer Scores for the same applications (e.g., applications discussed in two or more panels).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be cautious with small sample sizes (example: n=12) and consider adjusted significance thresholds; report t, df, p and effect direction (increase/decrease in range).

rubrics_metrics.name: Score Calibration Talk (SCT) — identification as analytic construct
rubrics_metrics.description: SCT: discourse instances where reviewers reference their own or others' scoring habits in order to establish common ground about the meaning of numeric scores; used as a mediator for understanding how discussion affects scoring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and count SCT instances and measure time spent. Use SCT (and its subtypes) as an explanatory variable in correlation analyses with score changes and convergence measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-initiated Score Calibration Talk (S-SCT) — definition
rubrics_metrics.description: S-SCT: any instance of discourse during which reviewers mention their scores (either the word 'score' or the number itself) along with an account (i.e. the rationale or justification) for that score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not code mere announcements like 'I gave it a four' as S-SCT unless accompanied by an account such as 'The reason I gave it a four was mainly due to problems with the approach.' S-SCT provides public access to an individual's interpretation of the numeric scale and can ground scores relative to application features or other reviewers' assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other-initiated Score Calibration Talk (O-SCT) — definition
rubrics_metrics.description: O-SCT: any instance of discourse during which one panelist calls on other reviewers to account for their scoring practices by offering a 'challenge' to their score (analytically borrowing 'challenge' from Conversation Analysis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat questions intended as challenges (e.g., known-answer questions or upshot formulations) as O-SCT. Do not code neutral information requests (e.g., 'What was your score again?') as O-SCT unless they function as a challenge. O-SCT is strongly associated with reviewers changing their scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coding and counting SCT instances and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: SCT instances are counted and timed (minutes:seconds) separately for S-SCT and O-SCT, and totals reported per meeting/panel (e.g., Table 4 showing counts and times for CSS1–CSS4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow explicit transcript-based coding rules (see Supplementary Appendix C). Note that SCT can span applications and speakers; this complicates per-application attribution. Report both raw counts and total time spent as analytic measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correlation analyses linking SCT to score change metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute correlations (Pearson r) between counts/time of SCT (Total, S-SCT, O-SCT) and (a) number of times reviewers changed their scores during meetings, and (b) percent of possible score-change events. Example results: Total SCT r=0.717 with score change; S-SCT r=0.107; O-SCT r=0.978.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret strong correlations (especially for O-SCT) as evidence that challenges are associated with score changes, but be cautious due to small sample sizes (e.g., only eight data points in some analyses). Repeat analyses using percent measures and time-based measures for robustness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correlation analyses linking SCT to score convergence (range differences)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute correlations between SCT counts/time and the change in within-panel range (range_final − range_prelim) to assess relationship with score convergence. Example: Total SCT r=0.980 for raw count; S-SCT r=0.682; O-SCT r=0.858.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use both raw counts and time-based SCT measures. Findings suggest SCT (especially O-SCT) is associated with within-panel convergence, while S-SCT has a stronger relationship with convergence than with mere score-change frequency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion criterion: only discussed applications have final scores
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyses of final scores and pre/post changes include only applications that were discussed in meetings (roughly the top-scoring 50%), because only those receive final scores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When planning analyses, restrict final-score comparisons to discussed applications and report this restriction and its implications for generalizability and sample composition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate both within-panel agreement and between-panel agreement separately
rubrics_metrics.description: Collaboration tends to reduce variability among reviewers within a panel (intra-panel convergence) but does not necessarily reduce—and may increase—variability between separate panels assessing the same applications (inter-panel divergence).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report intra-panel and inter-panel measures separately (e.g., ranges and Krippendorff's α). Do not assume that within-group consensus implies across-group reliability; consider both when assessing peer review reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretive constraints and analytic caveats (small samples, non-independence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Small number of panels, applications, and reviewers limit strong inferences; low counts of SCT per application restrict per-application correlation analyses; SCT episodes may span applications making independence assumptions invalid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid overinterpreting correlations from very small samples. Prefer aggregation at the meeting/panel level when individual-application independence is questionable. Recommend larger experimental/longitudinal designs to draw causal conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical interventions proposed to enhance reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Potential interventions include (a) a jigsaw technique where reviewers mix across groups to allow 'osmosis' of SCT and score norming, and (b) presenting 'standard' benchmark applications to all study sections to serve as scoring benchmarks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat these as testable operational interventions to reduce subjective variance across panels; pilot and experimentally evaluate effectiveness before large-scale adoption.
